Site restoration violations are also cited in this Notice of Violation. The well site has not been restored to post-construction stage.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/25/2024
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8184831
Permit API: 125-28816
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8234372
Permit API: 125-27157
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Independence Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/14/2025
Comments: On May 14, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Fred Jones well site in Independence Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination request was approved for this site on January 5, 2017. Dylan Stanley, Expand Energy Lease Operator, was onsite during this inspection. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the eastern cutslope of the well pad, which was reported to the DEP by the Expand Energy representative Jared Shockey on May 7, 2025. The DEP spoke Mr. Shockey on May 12, 2025, who stated that Expand Energy recently acquired this site and discovered the reported slough on the eastern cutslope upon assessing the site after acquisition. The slough is reportedly 1.5 feet deep and 100 feet long by 40 feet wide. The operator proposes to remove the sloughed material and add R4 riprap in its place as permanent stabilization.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). However, it appears to be heavily deteriorated with cracks forming in its reflective layer. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan are onsite. However, they are severely waterlogged and could not be evaluated during this inspection (see photo 2). GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a (see photo 16). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 17). Some rainwater was observed in the secondary containment of the production tanks (see photo 18). Well 206H appears to be equipped for production with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it observed (see photo 19). The faded well tag is completely illegible (see photo 20). There are two additional well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photos 21-24). The DEP spoke with Mr. Stanley onsite who stated that an order has already been placed for replacement well tags. The DEP recommended that the secondary containment of the production tanks is kept empty so it can function property in the event of a release. The DEP also recommended replacing the Act 9 sign and ERP onsite to ensure continued compliance post acquisition of site.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed (see photo 3). The slough that was reported by the operator on 5/07/2025 is present on the eastern cutslope of well pad. Its size appears to fit the dimensions reported by the operator. It does not appear to pose a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth at the time of inspection. A toe bulge was observed below the slough and possible additional cracking was observed at the southern end of the slough (see photos 5-15).Based on observations from this inspection, the DEP recommends that the operator install a new Act 9 sign, well tags, ERP, and PPC plan that are updated with the information of the current operator and comply with current regulations. The DEP also recommends that the operator monitor the slough on the eastern cutslope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on exposed soil.Violations shall be issued against the slough on the eastern cutslope of the well pad.The following information is requested from the operator:- What is being done in the interim (temporary stabilization)- What is being done in the future (permanent stabilization)If a Geotechnical Report would be necessary and/or developed for the soil crack and/or slough, please submit to DEP Technical Services. The Department recommends that the Operator coordinate with DEP Technical Services for any potential modifications to the approved ESCGP plans that may be necessary for addressing the soil crack and/or slough.

Comments: On 10/30/25 Oil and gas inspector Chuck Reaggle conducted a compliance schedule evaluation inspection of the HUMBERSTON UNIT 1H OG Well Permit number 051-24367. An Act 9 sign, Emergency response plan, and erosion and sediment control plans are present at the site entrance. At the time of inspection, I met with Moody and associates, INC representative Project manager Mr. Matt Kapral to observe soil gas readings being taken. Moody and associates took 20 soil readings utilizing their Bascom-Turner EGA-611. Points were every 5' from the well up to 25' to the north, south, east, and west. The results of the soil readings had the highest detection of methane gas from the soils at north 20' @ 7,040 parts per million at peak. And 180 parts per million sustained. (Picture 9). Moody and associates also took a reading utilizing their Bascom-Turner EGA-611 at the well casing isolated from the surrounding atmosphere and detected 25 Parts per million of carbon monoxide. 86% Methane. 4.1% Oxygen. And 0 Parts per million of hydrogen sulfide. Two isotopic samples were also taken from the isolated casing. (Pictures 7 and 8). Moody and associates took a soil gas readings from each corner of the well pad utilizing their Bascom-Turner EGA-611. "Zero" peak readings and "zero" sustained readings of methane gas was observed at the corners. (Picture 9). Utilizing the departments Bascom-Turner EGA-411, I observed the following readings at the well, 60 Parts per million of carbon monoxide. 58% Methane. 9.5% Oxygen. (Picture 3).

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chevron Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-01-10
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 873922
Permit API: 129-28979
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-01-10
Comments: As documented in Inspection Record #2971125, the self-reported amount of oil-based mud released was 5 barrels (see Spill/Release Information of Photo #2). The Department recommended remediating the spill pursuant to §78a66(c)2 in an Inspection received by the operator on December 13, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, a satisfactory initial written report pursuant to §78a66(c)2 has not been received. The report provided by the operator on December 12, 2019 and documented in Inspection Record #2971125 only satisfies §78a66(c)2(i)(A), (C), and (F). Inspection Records #2970703 and #2971139 shows petroleum-based mud in multiple locations on the pad. Inspection Record #2971139 shows an unknown substance with a rainbow sheen discharging from under secondary containment at least 100 feet from the well heads. The Department collected multiple sample on the site on December 6, 2019. Sample results show the petroleum-based mud in an erosion rill greater than 200 feet from the well heads. The rill is on the edge of the well pad and discharges toward a stormwater channel which leads to the PCSM forebay; this evidence is sufficient to not only show the extent of the spill, but also that the spilled material has left the well pad and entered stormwater facilities. Per a telephone conversation with Chevron representative B. A. Lambie on January 8, 2020, the initial remediation by Chevron was completed on December 9, 2019. Department personnel were on-site on December 9, 2019 as documented in Inspection Record #298131. At the time of inspection, secondary containment was still in place. A strong petroleum odor and non-bacterial sheen were observed near and in stormwater channel R-4, respectively. The Department collected multiple samples from the site on December 27, 2019. The rill and nearby areas had not been altered as of December 27, 2019, nor had channel R-4. Sample results from December 27, 2019 show hexane is present in at least three locations in the material spilled near the pad entrance as mentioned in Inspection Record #2970703. The spilled material will need remediated pursuant to §78a66(c). At this time, hexane is being treated as a separate spill. Additional violations are being issued. Photographs are referenced as part of the operator-provided inspections provided on December 16, 2019 as requested in Inspection Record #2971139. However, the photographs cannot be accessed. Therefore, the inspections provided were incomplete. The photographs were requested via e-mail on December 17, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the photographs have not been provided. Additional violations may be forthcoming based on review of the complete inspections. In Inspection Record #2971139, the Department requested photographic documentation of the removal of the secondary containment that remained on December 6, 2019 be provided by December 27, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the documentation has not been provided.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Barrett 410 well pad located in Jackson Township, Tioga County on 12/29/2025 at 1025 hours. The weather was 41 degrees F with mostly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator.On 12/24/2025, Repsol reported to the DEP via the reporting hotline that an estimated 23 gallons of produced fluids were released to the soil/gravel after the dump line for the produced fluids separated. Repsol reported that the impacted soil/gravel was recovered and that a third party company would visit on Friday, 12/26/2025, to verify that cleanup was complete. During my inspection, evidence of remediation was observed off the western fill slope (photo #6). The dump line appears to have a temporary repair in place (photo #5) with tape over the damage line. A bucket is located below the line to collect any additional leaks. Repsol reported that a permanent repair is scheduled for the near future. Any fluids and soils in and around the remediated area showed no evidence of any portion of the release remaining. Based on the findings of this inspection report, the reported release of produced fluids outside of secondary containment and Repsol's timely remediation, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-20391:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)SWMA 301I departed the site at 1135 hours.

Comments: On February 6, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the PF Eisaman South 43 Well Site (NOT previously approved on 6/6/2025) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/6/2026 (CTS 394994). Present during the inspection were operator representatives D.J Menas and Bruce Carpenter.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. Site stabilization could not be assessed due to snow cover.At the time of inspection, there are 6 total wells on the well pad. All wells appeared equipped for production with a well tag present. No fluid leaks or spills were identified at the surface around any of the well heads or cellars. The GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Carpenter guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Carpenter the release occurred earlier in the morning on 2/6/2026 when a worker was filling a day tank in their truck with diesel from the diesel tank on the pad (photo 4). Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2019-04-12
Comments: On Thursday April 11, 2019 at or about 1428 hours, I spoke on the telephone with Mr. David Guidas from EQT Production Company (EQT) regarding a release of impaired water that had been discovered approximately one hour prior to the telephone conversation. It was estimated that approximately three barrels (minimum) of impaired water had been released during hydraulic fracturing operations and exited containment at the Beta Cameron Well Site located in Richhill Township, Greene County. On Friday April 12, 2019 I conducted an incident inspection to further assess the situation. Mr. David Guidas along with other EQT personnel and the remediation contractor were also present during the inspection. At the time of the inspection, EQT had surmised that impaired water associated with the blender had leaked through secondary containment and impacted gravel in two locations along the side of the containment. The first area, located in closer proximity of the sand tanks had been delineated and remediated prior to the inspection. A soil conductivity probe was used to delineate the impacted area prior to removal of the material for off-site disposal. The soil conductivity probe was then used to confirm that all impacted material had been removed. The second area, located farther along containment from the first, was being remediated at the time of inspection. Contractors were removing standing fluid with a vacuum and the surface gravel had been scraped from the surface. Given that all details of the release are not known, EQT will continue to monitor the second location throughout the remaining stages of well stimulation. Any standing water will be immediately vacuumed into a truck and new stone will be used to construct a berm around the impacted area. It was estimated that the remaining stages will be completed in approximately seven to eight days. At the completion of the hydraulic fracturing activities, EQT will be able to move equipment and containment from the area in order to conduct a more thorough investigation to determine the extent of impact. Following the investigation, the impacted area will be fully remediated in accordance with Act 2 Guidelines and all impacted materials disposed accordingly. The release of impaired water which leaked through secondary containment and impacted gravel on the well pad is a violation of 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.54 and 35 P.S. Section 6018.301. EQT should respond in accordance with instructions provided in this notice.

Comments: On January 10, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad in response to a spill notification received on January 10, 2022. DEP spoke with Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources. Mr. Rodriguez said that a hose that manifolded multiple frac tanks onsite broke and released approximately 1,600 barrels of production fluid water from frac tanks. There were 17 frac tanks onsite in secondary containment for flow back storage from recent stimulation of the wells on the pad. The secondary containment of the frac tanks was overwhelmed and some of the production fluid water spilled to the pad surface. The amount of production fluid that was spilled to the pad surface is still being calculated. The spill was first noticed on January 8, 2022 but STL Resources failed to notify the DEP emergency spill line. The production fluid ran into a drain on the southwest corner of the well pad which outlets off the pad into a infiltration berm. An area 60 yds. x 40 yds. of the pad surface was impacted by production fluid. Off the pad area of impact was about 20 ft. wide by 120 ft. long. At the time of inspection, STL Resources contractors were vacuuming up the free standing production fluid out of the drainage outlet and the fluid pooled up in front of the infiltration berm. The DEP measured soil conductivity around the area of impact on the well pad and multiple measurements resulted in over range readings of the soil conductivity meter. Soil conductivity off the pad surface where the production fluid water flowed into the infiltration berm also resulted in an over range readings. The maximum conductivity measurement of the soil conductivity meter is 4,000 microsiemens per centimeter. STL Resources have contractors scheduled to arrive today to delineate the area of impact and to remove the impacted soils. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), Chapter 78a.66(b)2, Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends STL Resources begin the Act 2 process.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after the operator reported that on 3/3/23, an estimated 50 barrels of produced fluid was released on and off of secondary containment. The area surrounding the well pad and access road was snow-covered during this inspection. DEP Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Sean VanFleet accompanied me during this inspection. The frac was on-going during this inspection. Company man Matt Casler accompanied us at the beginning of the inspection in order to show us the location of the produced fluid release from 3/3/23. The area where the fluid released sprayed onto the pad surface is the area east of the modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) and the travel lane which runs along the southcentral edge of the pad. According to the company man, approximately 4 inches of material was scraped from the surface of the pad in these areas and had been hauled off site. No fluid was observed in this area. Mr. Casler also stated that no fluid or staining was observed on the south pad side slope immediately after the release. No fluid or staining was observed on the pad side slope or at the toe of the slope during this inspection.At the north corner of the pad at the outlet of the stormwater channel, the stormwater has an electrical conductivity (EC) of approximately 440 uS/cm. In the secondary containment at the west corner of the pad, adjacent to the MASS, fluid is present with an EC of 6.25 mS/cm. The produced fluid offload area at the southeast corner of the pad has fluid within it which has an EC of 3.00 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming out these containments. Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release which occurred on 3/3/23.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an Administrative (ADMIN) inspection of the Seneca Resources - Cruttenden 846 Well Site in response to receipt of a NOV response from the operator on 5/26/23 regarding violations of SWMA 301, 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a) and the violation of CSL 402(b), originally cited 1/11/23 in IR#3486282 and 2/17/23 in IR#3506790. The NOV response state "Per your request in Inspection Report [3486282], non-reportable, de minimis quantities of higher conductivity fluid were transferred by field personnel and truck tires. Using the collection bottle for scale in Photo #13, the puddle from which sample 4427-298 was collected is approximately 160 inches long by 40 inches wide by 1 inch deep, giving a total puddle volume of 87 gallons or 330 liters. Assuming a brine chloride concentration of 115,200 mg/L (chloride concentration averaged across eleven different 26R samples recently collected from eleven different wells in Tioga County), less than 2 gallons of brine would be necessary to produce the reported chloride concentrations in the puddle. The 2-gallon volume of brine is likely an overestimation given that the calculation assumes all the chloride comes from the brine and neglects the appreciable contribution of chloride expected from road salt. The chloride/barium ratio of 765 supports that the puddle is enriched with another source of chloride as the Tioga brine chloride/barium ratio averages around 20 (as calculated from the 26R samples referenced above). Given that the pad material is sourced from the limestone of the Benner through Loysburg Formations at the Salona Quarry in Mill Hall, a quarry frequented by local mineral clubs for its strontianite, strontium leaching from the limestone and concentrating in the clay fractions of the pad material is not unexpected. There was not a release of a reportable quantity of brine.The puddle volume from which sample 4427-295 was collected cannot be estimated as the puddle from which the sample is collected is not identified. Photo #9 refers to multiple puddles with varying levels of conductivity. The reported chloride concentration for sample 4427-295 is 5 times less than the chloride concentration from sample 4427-298. The chloride/barium ratio for this sample is 2,697, indicating that the sample is significantly enriched by a source of chloride other than brine. This puddle is believed to be road salt transfer. As described above, strontium leaching from the limestone and concentrating in the clay fractions of the pad material is not unexpected. There was not a release of a reportable quantity of brine. As a prudent and diligent operator, Seneca reports all reportable spills/releases per the PADEPs regulations. Seneca Operations staff are working with field staff and contractors to continually improve containment maintenance and pad conditions after precipitation events, especially in the winter months when freeze/thaw weather conditions are prevalent."The Operator's response will be uploaded to eFacts and a Compliance Evaluation Inspection will be conducted to evaluate the remediation of the release.Violations of the following regulations are cited as OUTSTANDING against the Cruttenden 846 34HU, API#117-22129 :SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)The violation of CSL 402(b), originally cited 1/11/23 in IR#3486282 and 2/17/23 in IR#3506790.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 8/20/2025 at 0830 hours. The weather was 62 degrees F with rain. The inspection was conducted to assess ongoing remedial activities after a well control incident on 7/13/2025 resulted in a produced fluids release.No remediation excavation activities were occurring today due to the rain. Impacted materials stored within secondary containment (photo #2) continue to be loaded into trucks and hauled offsite for disposal. An interceptor trench was installed around the entire secondary containment on the pad surface that collects fluids and diverts them into a pipe (photo #1) that eventually flows into the trench below the pad's fill slope. Fluids were flowing into the lined detention basin from both the eastern and western lined channels today (photos #5 and 6). Fluids flowing in the western channel were field measured at ~6mS/cm and fluids flowing the in the eastern channel were field measured at ~370us/cm. Less than 6 inches of fluids were currently held in the lined detention basin (photo #4).Resource Environmental collected samples from the three shallow, monitoring wells drilled downslope of the well pad on 8/7/2025. Repsol reported that the samples collected on 8/7/2025 from Monitoring Well (MW) MW04A showed that elevated constituents were reported. MW04A can be seen in photo #10 and is located downslope of the preexisting stormwater basin. During remediation of the preexisting stormwater basin, a large rock was removed and a ~4-inch borehole was discovered beneath the basin (photo #9). Repsol reported that the borehole was ~27 feet deep and was not discovered during construction because it is located on the fill side of the basin and was ~3 feet beneath the native soils. It is unclear at this time if the borehole is causing the elevated constituents found in MW04A. Resource Environmental continues weekly sampling from the three shallow, monitoring wells, streams and various seeps on the fill slope. Repsol intends to have confirmatory samples collected from the soils in the remediated stormwater basin, and then backfill, however, a permanent structure will be installed to allow continued access to the discovered borehole. Resource Environmental was screening and purging fluids from the borehole today. Shallow, monitoring well MW01A has not been drilled yet. A rig is tentatively scheduled for drilling of MW01A and the four deep monitoring wells sometime next week. A puddle within the remediated basin (photo #8) returned a field measured reading of ~360us/cm.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: On 01/06/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Rough Hollow Well Site following receipt of a spill reported to the Department on 01/05/2026 (CTS 394427). I was accompanied by Ralph Barb and Laura Grada (PA DEP).The operator reported that approximately 5-10 gallons of production fluid was released to the pad. No waterways were affected and SPSI (cleanup crew) was on site.The Department contacted the operator on 01/06/2026 prior to inspection and received the following information:The release occurred within the GPU. The dump line failed within the unit.The release occurred within the gas production unit (GPU) associated with the Rough Hollow 593213- 12HU well (API - 059-27108). This wells GPU is not listed within the secondary containment Consent Order and Agreement (COA).The well was SPUD on 09/30/2016.The operator determined the amount released visually; however, they are working to determine the exact amount that was released.Excavation is on hold until the operator can determine the exact quantity released and if additional excavation is necessary.The following was observed during inspection on 01/06/2026:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was on site (Photos 1, 2).The spill was observed adjacent to GPU 12H. The impacted area was excavated and sumps dug. The GPU did not appear to be on secondary containment (Photos 3-6).Conductivity readings were obtained adjacent to the excavated area and within the sumps and excavated area. The readings adjacent to the excavated area ranged from 76.9 - 1945 S/cm (Photos 7-10). The readings within the sumps and excavated area ranged from 4.36 - 18.80 mS/cm (Photos 11-15).Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the release of production fluid.

Comments: On the afternoon of July 8, 2026 I was contacted by the PA Game Commission (PGC) regarding a potential brine leak found on SGL 87. PGC provided me with photos and GPS coordinates.I notified the operator, Diversified Production LLC, on the morning of July 9, 2026. Will Warfel of Diversified met me onsite at conventional well 033-24578. A Diversified pipeline is located nearby this conventional well. Downslope from this conventional well, a 30 BBL brine tank is stationed and connected to the Diversified pipeline. We discovered that an animal had chewed a hole through the bottom of the brine tank, resulting in an unknown amount of brine fluids released. I screened the area using a Hanna soil probe, elevated conductivity readings >4.00 mS/cm were found close by the brine tank. Dead vegetation and elevated conductivity readings were found traveling approximately 15 feet from the brine tank.Mr. Warfel had a backhoe onsite during the time of the inspection. Compost sock was being delivered today as well. Mr. Warfel stated they will proceed with site remediation via the Act 2 process since the operator is uncertain of the amount of brine fluids released.Violations have been cited.

Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for broken and corroded piping and a release from broken and corroded piping.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4106039, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department attempted to contact the Operator by calling the number posted on the well tag, however, the number was not in service, therefore violations are being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate information posted on the well posting.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank under/adjacent to the corroded pipes. Although, these soil conductivity readings (0.0328 mS, 0.0899 mS, and 0.0244 mS) are not elevated, it does not visual appear that the release that previously occurred has yet to be remediated as vegetation in this area appears to be distressed and the gravel in this area is stained. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping is to remain outstanding at this time and new violations are being issued at this time for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2018-12-04
Comments: Arrived onsite at 10:43 in response to a spill notification received on 12/3/18 at 15:45. Peg Farrell reported a release of about 25 gallons of brine water off of containment at the northeast corner of the pad near the produced water tanks and sand vac. The impacted area included a portion of the a collection ditch at the edge of the pad. Chief was in the process of stimulating the 4H well. Met with Colter, Company Man onsite and Kellon, Environmental Field Coordinator. They believed the cause of the spill to be from an overflowed blender. The overflow then leaked through containment and onto the pad surface. There are two layers of containment under the equipment (plastic, felt, plastic, felt). Chief will continue to inspect the containment during operations and repair any punctures or tears found. The vac truck onsite removed pooled water from the containment as soon as the spill was noticed. At the time of inspection an excavator was removing the impacted area of the pad. The area being excavated was approximately 8 ft. wide, 15 ft. long, and 2 in. deep (Photo #1). At the time of inspection about 10 to 15 cubic feet of soil had been removed. It was expected that 20 to 25 cubic feet would be removed in total. A Hanna Instruments Soil Conductivity Tester (S/N: L02110754) was used to screen the nearby area and it appeared that contamination was limited to the area immediately around the excavation (Photos #2, 3). The 5H well is scheduled to be stimulated following the 4H. Operations are expected to be completed Sunday afternoon (12/9/18). Chief is planning to pull additional containment under the blender and around the contaminated area the following Monday or Tuesday (12/10 or 12/11) to conduct additional screening of the pad surface. Violations noted and immediately corrected.

Comments: Site inspection conducted at the COP Tract 551B pad to review use of EWS VOX4 evaporators for processing flowback water. Meeting on site today with EWS representative Pat Pascarella. There are no EQT personnel on site at time of inspection. A TetraTek crew is loading produced fluid into water trucks. Weather conditions are partly sunny and 73 degrees F. Wind is blowing from the southwest at an estimated 5 mph. Eight EWS Vox4 evaporators are in use at time of inspection. Evaporators process fluid in batches, with automated systems in use to pump water into the system from the production fluid tanks and out to the frac tank batteries when fluid is concentrated. All pipelines and fluid control systems appear to be functioning as designed and there is no fluid or precipitation within evaporator containment. As authorized under the Air Quality Request for Determination Operating Permit, EQT will take four evaporators out of service after the initial 60 days of use. According to Mr. Pascarella, four units will be disconnected on June 13. There are no violations associated with the evaporator authorization. Fluid with elevated conductivity (3.14 mS/cm) is still present at the NE pad sump (photo 7). Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Seneca Resources' DeCristo (01-128) D well site located in Sullivan Township, Bradford County on 9/16/2025 at 1115 hours. The weather was 69 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported discovered release. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #392245 is tied to the release within CTS.The eight active well permits and erosion and sediment control general permit currently list Seneca Resources (Seneca) as the operator. Repsol Oil and Gas (Repsol) is currently handling overlook of some operations during flowback, including the offloading and transportation of produced water from the site. Seneca and Repsol are currently working on transferring the permits back to Repsol. On 9/15/2025, Repsol contacted the DEP to report that during screening efforts prior to transferring the permits back to Repsol, a consultant (WSP) discovered an area on the pad surface where a suspected release of produced water occurred. The suspected release was discovered on 9/12/2025. Repsol reported that the release quantity was unknown but calculations determined that the release was likely more than a barrel. The release was determined to be located in front of the produced water tanks' offload area and was spread linearly across the pad surface towards the "exit" of the pad (photos #2 and 3). Since the site's and wells' permits are currently under Seneca ownership, I recommended that Seneca report the release to the DEP. Seneca contacted the DEP reporting hotline on 9/15/2025 to report the discovery of the suspected release on behalf of Seneca. Seneca reported that the exact time of the release was unknown but is assumed to have occurred during flowback. The suspected release was discovered due to elevated electrical conductivity readings noted during the pad assessment which was conducted by WSP.During today's inspection, it was observed that the release had already been remediated. No evidence of any spills/releases was observed. The areas remediated have already been backfilled and were dry today (photos #2 and 3). Based on the reported discovery of a release of an unknown quantity outside of secondary containment, violations of the following are cited against API #117-22244 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed the site at 1245 hours.

Comments: This site located in a pasture field, north of intersection of MacAdam and Dairy Roads, across Dairy Road from a barn on a short access through a gate into pasture. This well set-up for production with a meter(broken) and a tank with no secondary containment. Paul Stiner reported a release of ~40 barrels of produced fluid, oil and brine, to ground from the tank at this well. The release was caused as a result of the discharged valve on the tank broken off by cattle in the pasture, there is no fence or barrier around the well to prevent access to well head and production equipment by livestock. The tank was loaded on a truck and removed from site at the time of this inspection. There was oil under the west edge of where the tank had been located and a path of oil saturated soil 40'-50' west of the tank. There is a ~100' path of dead vegetation that includes the oily area. Diversified well tender and trainee on site, Diversified employee marking pipeline also on site. Clean-up to begin when equipment arrives on site today.

Report Details

Violation ID: 922658
Permit API: 053-27124
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/08/2021
Comments: Responded to a call from Minard Run to Scott Motter ( Dep representative) in regards that there had been a crude oil spill at one of there tank batteries in Forest County, Howe Township PA. Upon arriving on location I met with Minard Run Representative Gary Davis and USFS Mike Lewis. They gave a brief run down of the incident and work that had been completed to stop the flow of Crude Oil. There was a failure at well 053-27124. A valve broke which was connected to a steel line on the exit side of the check valve, which is going to tank battery. Minard Run is on site. A new valve was installed. Booms and pads were in place at the time of my arrival. They are Currently digging diversion ditches and a siphon dam. Crude product left the well site, traveled the road ditch, and went through a culvert. At that point some of the product went into a fresh water pond and some oil diverted around the pond into a wet land and then into a wooded area. Once it entered the wooded area the product penetrated the large rock structure area and flowed underground to the fresh water tributary. Pictures show where Minard Run placed booms to attempt to stop the flow down stream. The flow is carrying some product further down stream, in which they have more booms in place. It was approx estimate of 2 to 3 barrels of crude leaked. Minard Run was going to try to get a volume of the gathering lines to help identify the volume. It was suggested to add additional booms down stream and continue with the current clean up process. In light of future rains tonight it was suggested to leave booms in-place and remove pads to prevent them being pushed down stream. Minard Run did an excellent job responding and attempting to clean up the oil in the early stages of the incident. This will be forwarded to WQS for follow up.

Violation ID: 8169729
Permit API: 129-27066
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/27/2023
Comments: December 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill reported to the Department on 10/20/2023 (CTS: 375673). According to the operator, the spill was approximately 40 barrels of production fluid, released from the valve near the bottom of the production tank. The initial inspection of the spill is documented in IR 3636824. The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the production tank appeared to be removed from the site and it appeared that excavation of the contaminated material had begun. The area of excavation was approximately 30 feet by 30 feet and roughly 5.5 feet in depth. The Department took conductivity readings at the bottom of the excavated area with readings of 0.02mS, 0.12mS, and 0.18mS. It appeared that all of the excavated material was still on site, in several piles surrounding the excavated hole. In some areas, it appeared sediment had begun to travel downslope from the piles. Upon further inspection, it appeared that no E and S BMPs were implemented anywhere on the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Previous violations associated with the release remain outstanding.
